coverage.assessment: Carter's warning loses Tommy's 'tips' prompt and the 'don't be discouraged... For one thing' logic. Julius's reason for coming to England (Jane unheard of; officials not hustling) is cut. The coincidence theme, the terms, the salary, the taxi and the blackmailer joke are all intact.

In Tuppence's complaint, 'they send us' has lost its referent, 'the Government'. The lunch location is vague but harmless. The 'this morning' visit, Japp's card at lunch and Paris 'to-morrow' are all preserved.
The question 'When did you last see your cousin?' has no speaker; the source gives it to Tuppence. Tommy's shared realisation is folded into a monologue. Other turns remain clear.
Thirty-five, three hundred a year each, 'only copy in existence', and 'Scotland Yard again. Another man this time' are kept exactly. 'Buy her off' keeps an implied condition.
The ending stops at 'Quiet, unassuming sort of chap.' Nothing from 007 is imported, and nothing hints where the photograph is or casts doubt on Julius.

Narratorial touches such as 'Mr. Beresford obliged' and 'nodded sagely' survive, as do the steel image and 'I'm not sure I have'. Carter's hedged consolation, Tuppence's 'devil of a time', and Julius's 'speed things up' and tremendous energy are trimmed.
Carter's double-edged view of the forced pace ('I hope it will myself') becomes a pure threat. Julius's forceful, moneyed impatience, which sets up later bribe offers, is weakened.
Dependencies 0–2 are intact at both endpoints. For dependency 3, the local account survives, but the 027 revision cut the 'went out West... photograph' sentence.

findings.claim: The revision cuts Tommy's request for tips. It also cuts Carter's 'imagination and an open mind... Don't be discouraged', the 'For one thing' connective, 'I hope it will myself', and 'needn't be cast down if you fail'. Carter now slides from fate straight to 'My experts have failed.' The forced-pace line reads as a bare threat rather than one reason not to despair, and Carter's own hope that haste will hurt the enemy is lost.
findings.counterevidence: The essential new-year coup, the strike legislation and 'haven't much time' all survive in revision paragraph 5.

strengths: The closing sting lands intact: the dread, the stammered question, Julius's 'Yes, I do. No, I don't' dithering, and 'Quiet, unassuming sort of chap.'
The coincidence theme is kept through Tuppence's 'meant to be' and Carter's admitted superstition.
Tommy murmurs Carter's real name without the text ever giving it, followed by 'he's IT!', the steel image, the pinch and 'Mr. Beresford obliged.'
The blackmailer joke keeps its dark capper: 'I'm not sure I have,' said Tuppence darkly.
summary: The revision is coherent and faithful in structure. All eight verbatim lines survive, the continuity checks hold, Carter's name stays unstated, and the Inspector Brown cliffhanger stays clean. The losses are editorial rather than blocking. Carter's warning loses its prompt and its consoling logic, so the 'pace being forced' line arrives abruptly. Tuppence's form complaint loses its Government antecedent. The detective-fiction question is now unattributed. Julius's hustling motive and the narrator's comment on his energy are thinned.
